problemes.titol: De què tracta el llibre *Au Pair*
problemes.text:
**WHAT THE AU PAIR SAW**

Silvia, an 18-year-old from Bratislava, the capital of Slovakia, could not believe how **mean** her employers were. They hardly spoke to her, made her work very long hours for very little pay and restricted her access to food. Silvia didn’t work in a shop. She was an au pair to a middle-class British family.

Silvia’s story comes from a new book, called *Au Pair*, which takes a full and honest look at British families from the sincere point of view of the girls who come to look after their children and help around the house.

The book focuses on the experiences of 50 Slovakian au pairs who have lived with more than 100 **host families** in London. Its author is Zuzana Burikova, a Slovakian sociologist who has been working on this project for more than three years.

The book’s most noticeable feature is the pejorative view that au pairs develop towards their host British families. In particular, they are highly critical of the *‘having it all’* culture. British **parenting**, it seems, is shockingly bad. The book suggests that the British concept of a woman’s right to a career as well as a family is viewed negatively by au pairs. The author thinks that “au pairs generally feel that any family that chooses to have an au pair must, by definition, either be lazy, or lack proper care and consideration for children and for people in general”.

In the book we can read about the experience of an au pair called Jarmila, whose host mother worked at home as a clothes designer. Even when she was not working, her child spent all his time with Jarmila, who really felt like a second mother. Another case is that of Darinka, who was fascinated by “English mothers constantly talking about quality time and feeling guilty if they were not actually reading to or playing with their children”. In fact, in most cases it was pretty clear they spent very little time with their children. “English women do love their children,” Darinka **reluctantly** admits, “but the problem is that they are just not able to combine childcare, housework and a career.”

From the experiences in the book we can learn that “food is a particularly tricky issue,” says Ms. Burikova. “I’m surprised that children and parents do not eat the same food and that parents buy healthy food like vegetables and fish for themselves but not for their children.” Zuzana Burikova explains that “the British like TV programmes where experts tell them how to keep their home, since they don’t know how to do it themselves. That’s why they need au pairs.”

And yet, as with all things, there is a **flip side**. And not all families are cold and unfeeling. In the book we can read the experience of Tina. Tina worked in London as an au pair about nine years ago. She had an absolutely terrific time in there, and there was good understanding between Tina and her host family, as a result of which the family decided to **put her up** until she finished her studies.

After having studied all these experiences, Zuzana Burikova comes to the conclusion that none of all these au pairs’ negative experiences stop people from applying for the job. Most Slovakian women go to Britain to work as an au pair in order to learn the language and earn some money at the same time, but there are also others that accept this job because it’s a way of escaping from their families or simply because they have just split up with their boyfriend. So, up to a point, the arrangement suits them.

*Text adapted from The Sunday Times (August 1, 2010)*

- **host family**: família d’acollida / familia de acogida
- **parenting**: criança / crianza
- **reluctantly**: a contracor / a su pesar
- **flip side**: l’altra cara de la moneda / la otra cara de la moneda
- **to put her up**: acollir-la, contractar-la / acogerla, contratarla

problemes.enunciat:
Choose ONE topic. Write about number 1 or 2. Minimum length: 100 words.

passos.cos: Opció 1 del writing (cal triar-ne una de les dues): una **carta formal de sol·licitud** adreçada a una agència d'au pairs. Mínim 100 paraules (apunta a 140-170; uns 25-30 minuts). La tasca central és explicar **per què ets la persona ideal** per a la feina: experiència amb nens, qualitats personals, idiomes, disponibilitat i motivació. Registre **formal**: sense contraccions (*I am*, no *I'm*), fórmules d'obertura i tancament formals. Pots aprofitar idees del reading (aprendre la llengua, guanyar diners, conviure amb una família d'acollida), però **no copiïs** frases del text.

Estructura:

1. **Salutació formal**: *Dear Sir or Madam,* (si no saps el nom) o *Dear Mrs Smith,*.
2. **Paràgraf 1 – motiu de la carta**: *I am writing to apply for a position as an au pair…*
3. **Paràgraf 2 – experiència i qualitats**: feina amb nens, monitor/a, germans petits, paciència, responsabilitat.
4. **Paràgraf 3 – altres punts forts i motivació**: idiomes, cuina, carnet de conduir, ganes d'aprendre anglès i de conèixer la cultura.
5. **Tancament**: disponibilitat, documents adjunts, *I look forward to hearing from you.*
6. **Comiat**: *Yours faithfully,* (amb *Dear Sir or Madam*) o *Yours sincerely,* (amb nom) + nom complet.

**Estructures i connectors útils**

- Obertura: *I am writing to apply for…, I saw your advertisement in…*
- Experiència: *I have been working as… for two years, I have experience in…*
- Qualitats: *I consider myself (patient / reliable / hard-working)…*
- Addició: *Furthermore, In addition, Moreover, Not only… but also…*
- Finalitat: *in order to…, so that…*
- Tancament: *I would be grateful if…, Please find attached my CV, I look forward to hearing from you.*

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to apply for a position as an au pair with a British family, which I saw advertised on your website.

I am eighteen years old and I have just finished my secondary education in Barcelona. I believe I would be the ideal person for this job because I have a lot of experience with children. For the last two summers I have worked as a monitor in a holiday camp, where I was responsible for groups of six-year-olds. Moreover, as the eldest of four brothers and sisters, I am used to helping with homework, cooking simple meals and keeping a house tidy.

I consider myself patient, reliable and cheerful. In addition, I can speak Catalan, Spanish and English, and I would be happy to teach the children a few words of my languages. My main aim is to improve my English and to learn about British culture while doing a job I really enjoy.

I am available from September. Please find attached my CV and two references.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,  
Laia Puig

La consigna té dues parts: (1) donar la teva **opinió** sobre si és millor treballar al teu país o a l'estranger i (2) explicar **avantatges o inconvenients de tots dos casos** (*in either case*). Registre neutre-formal, sense contraccions, amb paràgrafs clars i connectors. Pots aprofitar exemples del reading (les au pairs que van a Londres), però **no copiïs** frases.

Estructura:

1. **Introducció**: presenta el tema (cada cop més joves treballen a fora) i anuncia la teva postura.
2. **Paràgraf 2 – treballar a l'estranger**: avantatges (idiomes, experiència, independència, sous) i inconvenients (soledat, xoc cultural).
3. **Paràgraf 3 – treballar al propi país**: avantatges (família, amics, cultura pròpia) i inconvenients (menys oportunitats en temps de crisi).
4. **Conclusió**: la teva opinió final, amb un matís.

**Estructures i connectors útils**

- Opinió: *In my opinion, I strongly believe that, As far as I am concerned…*
- Avantatges i inconvenients: *One advantage of… is that…, The main drawback is…*
- Contrast: *On the one hand… on the other hand, However, Although, Whereas…*
- Exemples: *For example, For instance, such as…*
- Conclusió: *To sum up, All in all, In conclusion…*
- Estructures avançades: *It is worth + -ing, The more… the more…, Not only… but also…*

Nowadays more and more young people leave their country to find a job. Is it better to work abroad or to stay at home? In my opinion, working abroad for a few years is a great experience, although it is not for everybody.

On the one hand, working abroad has clear advantages. You learn a foreign language much faster, you become more independent and you get to know a different culture. Moreover, salaries are sometimes higher and there may be more job opportunities than at home. However, living far from your family and friends can be hard, and some people feel lonely or homesick.

On the other hand, working in your own country means you can stay close to the people you love and you do not have to adapt to a new way of life. The main drawback is that, in times of crisis, it can be very difficult to find a good job.

All in all, I believe it is worth working abroad for some time, as long as you come back with new skills to use in your own country.

problemes.titol: Correu electrònic a un amic sobre un viatge recent
problemes.enunciat:
Choose ONE topic. Write about number 1 or 2. Minimum length: 100 words.

[4 points]

**Topic 1.** Write an e-mail to a friend. Explain a trip you have done recently. Talk about the places you visited, when and who with. Mention any interesting or funny anecdotes that happened during the journey.

passos.cos: Opció 1 del writing (cal triar-ne una de les dues): un **correu electrònic informal** a un amic. Mínim 100 paraules (apunta a 140-170; uns 25-30 minuts). La consigna té **quatre punts** i cal cobrir-los tots: (1) **llocs** que vas visitar, (2) **quan**, (3) **amb qui** i (4) una **anècdota** interessant o divertida. Registre informal (contraccions, salutació i comiat amistosos) però gramàtica correcta. Narra en **passat** (simple i continu) i fes servir connectors temporals. Pots inspirar-te en el reading (el Camí de Sant Jaume), però **no copiïs** frases.

Estructura:

1. **Salutació** (*Hi Tom,*) i **obertura**: per què escrius (acabes de tornar d'un viatge).
2. **Paràgraf 1 – quan, amb qui i on**: dates, companys de viatge i ruta.
3. **Paràgraf 2 – llocs visitats** i què et van semblar.
4. **Paràgraf 3 – l'anècdota**: narra-la amb passat continu + passat simple (*While we were…, suddenly…*).
5. **Tancament i comiat** (*Write soon! / Love, / Take care,*) i nom.

**Estructures i connectors útils**

- Passat simple i continu: *We set off…, While we were walking, it started to rain…*
- Connectors temporals: *First, Then, After that, The next day, Finally, In the end…*
- Emocions: *It was amazing!, I've never laughed so much, You won't believe what happened…*
- Present perfect per a experiències: *I've just come back from…*
- Expressions informals: *Guess what!, Anyway, By the way, Write soon!*

Hi Tom,

How are you? I've just come back from an amazing trip and I couldn't wait to tell you about it.

Last month, during the Easter holidays, my cousin Marc and I walked the last part of the Camino de Santiago. We started in Sarria and it took us six days to reach Santiago. On the way we visited lovely villages, old stone bridges and green forests, and every night we slept in a different hostel.

The funniest thing happened on the third day. While we were having lunch by a river, a cow came out of nowhere and ate Marc's sandwich! He was so shocked that he fell into the water. I laughed so much that I couldn't help him for a while. Luckily, it was a warm day and he dried quickly.

When we finally arrived in Santiago, we felt really proud. You should do it with me next summer!

Write soon,  
Anna

[4 points]

**Topic 2.** You are a journalist for a travel magazine. Write an article describing a place you know well. Mention the interesting things to see and do there. Un article porta **títol** atractiu, una introducció que enganxi i un to viu però correcte (pots adreçar-te al lector amb *you*). Tria un lloc que coneguis bé: et serà més fàcil donar detalls concrets.

Estructura:

1. **Títol** atractiu.
2. **Introducció**: presenta el lloc i desperta l'interès del lector (pregunta retòrica o frase impactant).
3. **Paràgraf 2 – història i cultura**: orígens, monuments, tradicions.
4. **Paràgraf 3 – què veure i fer**: llocs concrets, activitats, menjar.
5. **Paràgraf 4 – consells pràctics**: moneda, clima, horaris, costums locals.
6. **Conclusió**: recomanació final.

**Estructures i connectors útils**

- Descripció: *It is located…, It is famous for…, It is well worth a visit…*
- Passiva per a la història: *It was founded by…, The walls were built in…*
- Recomanacions: *Don't miss…, Make sure you…, You should / had better…*
- Superlatius: *one of the most beautiful…, the best time to visit…*
- Clima i costums: *Summers are hot, Bear in mind that…, Shops close at…*
- Connectors: *Moreover, Apart from…, However, Finally…*

**Girona: A Hidden Gem in Catalonia**

Looking for a city full of history but without the crowds of Barcelona? Then Girona is the place for you.

Girona was founded by the Romans more than two thousand years ago, and you can still walk along its medieval walls. Its old town has one of the best-preserved Jewish quarters in Europe, a beautiful Gothic cathedral and narrow stone streets where some scenes of famous TV series have been filmed.

There is plenty to see and do. Don't miss the colourful houses over the river Onyar, and try the local food, such as "botifarra" sausage. In May, the city celebrates "Temps de Flors", when streets and courtyards are decorated with flowers.

As for practical tips, the currency is the euro, and summers are hot, so bring a hat. Bear in mind that people have lunch at around two o'clock and many small shops close in the afternoon.

Girona is definitely worth a visit!

*(Introducció)* Famous for his jumpers and his relaxed behaviour, John Craven is one of the best-loved presenters on British television. He has been the presenter of the BBC television programmes **Newsround** and **Countryfile** and in 1996 the Royal Television Society made John Craven a member of its Hall of Fame. *(From a BBC Radio Interview. Adapted.)*

**Mary:** John, we are delighted to have you here. Welcome to our programme.

**John:** Thank you for inviting me. It’s a real pleasure.

**Mary:** Is it true that you only ever missed one episode of *Newsround* and that was because your wife was having a baby?

**John:** No, that's not exactly true. The first edition I missed was in the very early days, in 1972, when my first daughter was born and the newsreader Richard Whitmore took over for me. Later, I did miss two or three editions because of illness and when the programme went daily round the year, every week, I did take some holidays!

**Mary:** How did you start in the TV business?

**John:** Well, I left school at 16 and got a job as a commercial apprentice. But I was really more interested in writing than in studying to be a company secretary so after three years I became a junior reporter for a local newspaper. Maybe I should have studied harder and tried to get to university, but in those days you didn't need a degree to get into journalism and I had a great time in my early twenties learning my trade.
